overall: The AG found the Conservation Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by approving minutes late, failing to respond to two complaints, and members not completing certification forms; the website-posting allegation was declined.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Commission failed to approve meeting minutes in a timely manner on numerous occasions in 2020 and 2021.
allegations.key_passage: we noted several sets of minutes that were signed and dated by the Commission’s Chair between eight and twelve months after the corresponding meeting, well outside of the three meeting or 30-day requirement.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Commission failed to properly respond to two Open Meeting Law complaints filed with it.
allegations.key_passage: Here, we find no evidence that the Commission sent a response to Ms. Bicki, as required, nor did the Commission notify our office or provide a copy of the complaint and response.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged Commission members did not complete Open Meeting Law certification forms within two weeks of qualifying for office.
allegations.key_passage: we conclude that the Commission members violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to complete the required certification form.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Commission failed to post its 2020 and 2021 meeting minutes to the Wareham Town website.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require that public bodies post their minutes to a website or elsewhere, but only that minutes be approved in a timely manner and made available, if they exist, within 10 days of a request.

remedy: We order the Commission’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Create and approve, within 60 days of receipt, minutes for all 2020 and 2021 meetings lacking approved minutes, using the best available means including attendee memories and notes.
Send copies of all 2020 and 2021 meeting minutes to the complainant within 65 days of receipt and make them available to the public upon request.
Each Commission member must complete the Attorney General's Open Meeting Law certification form within two weeks of receipt of the letter.
remedy_passage: We order the Commission’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Commission that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
